key_insight: Large Language Models' internal (parametric) knowledge can be directly used to verify factual claims, enabling effective fact checking without relying on external retrieval pipelines.
problem_solved: Removes dependence on retrieval and external evidence sources for claim verification, addressing failure modes caused by missing or noisy retrieved documents and reducing latency and system complexity.
method: Prompt LLMs to assess claim veracity using their stored knowledge and reasoning capabilities rather than fetching external evidence.
Use structured verification prompts and verification-aware decoding (e.g., multi-step reasoning, calibration or self-consistency) to improve faithfulness and confidence estimation.
Evaluate and compare the retrieval-free pipeline to retrieval-based baselines across factuality benchmarks to validate feasibility and trade-offs.
impact: Offers a simpler, lower-latency fact-checking approach that is robust when external knowledge is unavailable, making trustworthy verification more practical for deployed AI systems and edge scenarios.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: Retrieval-based workflow vs. Retrieval-free (parametric) workflow highlighting removed components and shorter path to verdict.
Flowchart of the verification prompt process showing claim → reasoning steps → verdict + confidence.
Bar chart comparing latency and end-to-end dependency (external data) for retrieval vs. retrieval-free methods.
Icon set illustrating trade-offs: accuracy, latency, robustness to missing data, and calibration/confidence.
paper_title: Leveraging LLM Parametric Knowledge for Fact Checking without Retrieval
paper_authors: Artem Vazhentsev, Maria Marina, Daniil Moskovskiy, Sergey Pletenev, Mikhail Seleznyov
